dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. Good morning.
Morning. I'm calling about a recycling bin. It got left at my property with a tag on it saying it was rejected, and I need to know how to get a replacement.
Okay, I can help with that. So the bin was tagged as rejected. Is that the bin itself that's damaged, or the tag was about what was inside it?

The tag says rejected. That's all it says, more or less. There's a box checked, I'd have to look at it again. I'm not home right now, I'm out walking. I'm standing at a corner waiting to cross with a backpack that weighs a ton, so bear with me.
No problem at all, take your time. Be careful crossing. Let me get some details down while you're waiting. What's the address where the bin is?
130 Washington Street. Down the Point.
130 Washington Street, in the Point. Got it. And is that your own home, or are you the owner of a rental there?
I'm the landlord. I own the building. The tenants put the bin out, I didn't, but it's my account, so it's on me.
That's fine, I can work with the owner. Can I have your name?
Deirdre Hanlon. H-A-N-L-O-N.
Deirdre Hanlon, H-A-N-L-O-N. Thank you. Now, when was the bin tagged? Was it this past pickup?

It was this morning, I think. Or it was there when I went by. Monday pickup, anyway. After the storm, everything was a mess out there, last weekend's nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday. Maybe that's why the thing looks the way it does.
Okay, so Monday pickup, the day after the storm ended. Does the bin look damaged, cracked or missing a lid? Or did it just get left with the tag on it?
[pause] Hold on, the light changed. Okay, I'm crossing. Sorry. It's left. The bin is sitting there full, with the tag on the handle. Nothing's broken that I know of.

Alright. If it's still full and the tag is on it, that usually means the crew didn't empty it because of something in the load, or the bin wasn't set out right. The tag should say which. If you can read it to me when you're back, that tells us whether you need a replacement or just need to fix what's in it.
I figured it'd be a struggle. I don't want a lecture, I want a bin that works. How do I request a replacement, if that's what it comes to?

Understood. If the bin is damaged, lost, or the wrong kind, we put in a request for a replacement and a crew delivers it. I'll make that note on your account now so it's started. Do you want a replacement for sure, or only if the tag says the bin itself is the problem?
Put in for the replacement. The tenants say the lid doesn't close right anyway. It's been like that a while.

Okay, so the lid doesn't close properly, and the bin got tagged and left. I'll write it up as a replacement request for 130 Washington Street. Now, I'm going to repeat this back so we have it right. Deirdre Hanlon, owner, 130 Washington Street, Monday pickup, bin tagged rejected and not emptied, lid doesn't close, replacement requested. Is that right?
That's right.
Good. Do you want a number for a callback in case the delivery gets sorted out and we need to reach you?
401-555-0184. Got it. Is that a landline or a cell?
Landline. If I'm not there, the tenants can pick up, or leave a message.

Okay, I'll note that. Now, about the tagged bin. Until the new one comes, leave the old one at the curb or move it back by the house, whichever you prefer, just keep it where the crew can find it for the swap. Don't throw anything out of it until you've read the tag.
And what if the tag says it was contaminated? Then it's not about the bin, it's about what the tenants put in it.

Then the replacement is still going in, since the lid is a real issue, but your tenants would want to sort out what goes where before the next pickup so it doesn't get tagged again. The tag usually has a note about what was wrong. If it's not clear when you read it, call back and tell me what it says.
Fine. How long for the new bin?
Usually a few days to a week or so, a little longer when the crews are catching up after a storm like this one. It'll be dropped at the property, you don't need to be there.
A week. Okay. That's what I needed.
Anything else I can help with today, Ms. Hanlon?
No, that's it. Thank you.
You're welcome. Have a good rest of your day, and mind that backpack.
Goodbye.
